For odd n=2m-1, a folded tridiagonal chain has off-diagonals -sqrt((j+1)(n-j))/(2n), diagonal 3/2 except final 3/2 minus/plus m/(2n). Only that boundary bit changes. Endpoint measures are parity-conditioned binomial weights at energies 1+k/n; unlike N724 this pair is not nominally isospectral. Delta F(tau)=2 exp(-tau)[(1-exp(-tau/n))/2]^n, bounded by min{2*8^-n,2(beta/(2n))^n}. At t_n=pi n the return amplitudes are -/+1. The source bounds full snapshot trace distance using an explicit vector-tail identity, then an adaptive classically indexed pure-state fidelity lemma gives final distinguishability <=sqrt(N)d and N>=max{8^n,(2n/beta)^n}/18. Spectral-band rescaling extends the order to all sufficiently large target times.

Lagrange interpolation at real times in [0,min{beta,t}], with R=sqrt(t^2+min{beta,t}^2) and k=ceil(4eR), has error <=(2R)^(k+1)/(k+1)! and l1 amplification <=(2eR/min{beta,t})^k. Measuring the reference probability 1/(1+F) in [1/2,1], then using its Lipschitz inverse, gives the exponential-order upper copy bound. Sharper Q=Theta(sqrt(n)8^n) and fixed-beta Theta_beta(n^(3/2)(2n/beta)^n) concern the explicit binary family, not universal minimax leading constants. Snapshot preparation cost is separate from copy count; the contraction success is bounded below by 1/2 but its implementation is not supplied free.

The local bounded-coupling stoquastic free-spin realization has a unique product vacuum, constant ground gap and vacuum-plus-one-excitation trajectories of Schmidt rank at most two. [1,2] is the active one-excitation band; the full many-body bandwidth is extensive. Matched bulk rational rounding to O(1/n) norm accuracy costs O(log n) bits per entry and retains the lower-bound order with different constants. It does not preserve sharp binary constants or establish constant independent disorder tolerance. An additional last-site seed gives O(min{beta,1/64}^-2) copy discrimination independent of chain length, so the fixed-seed interface is load-bearing. A separate carefully specified coherent-preparation oracle corollary has an O(Nd) hybrid bound; copy constants and arbitrary-input propagator claims do not transfer.

This is the full-quantum-snapshot member of the inverse-information family alongside N724's noisy scalar observations. It does not resolve or depend on the near-convex Hamiltonian capital N716, N711/N712 Gibbs/readout claims or forward positive-kernel simulation interfaces. Perfect state transfer, binomial kernels, fidelity bounds, analytic continuation and imaginary-time no-fast-forwarding are credited antecedents. The original research note, code, captured diagnostics, requirements and manifest are recoverable. Independent correctness, historical originality, generic interacting/Gibbs scope, instrument feasibility and a major foundational capability remain unestablished.
